messages:
maria: quick q — we're onboarding an OIDC-based service account flow. i'm minting a short-lived token with audience 'redwood-api' via our idp and then instantiating the JS SDK with projectId='acme-prod'. i'm seeing sporadic 401s on long-lived streams, curious which layer should be authoritative for project/org scoping?

kevin: short answer: server enforces the token 'aud' first. the project/org mapping in the client is local metadata used for routing/metrics. if aud doesn't match what the backend expects you'll get rejected. do you have the exact token exchange and client init?

maria: here's the minimal flow i'm using:
```js
// exchange service key for OIDC token
const resp = await fetch('https://idp.example.com/oauth/token', { method: 'POST', body: 'grant_type=client_credentials&audience=redwood-api' })
const token = (await resp.json()).access_token

// SDK init
const client = new Redwood({ auth: { type: 'oidc', token: token }, projectId: 'acme-prod' })
// open streaming route
const s = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'gpt-4-lite', messages: [...] })
```

tariq: two practical gotchas we've hit: 1) audience mismatch as kevin said; 2) streaming connections (SSE/ws) do NOT magically swap headers mid-stream when you refresh a token. the connection keeps using the auth header that was set when it opened. so if your token expires while the stream is active you'll see a 401 from the gateway and the stream will drop. need to reconnect after refresh.

maria: ah that explains it — we were refreshing in the background but not reconnecting. what's the recommended pattern in the SDK?

jen: also watch token lifetime vs refresh timing. if the idp returns 1m tokens and your refresh window is aggressive but clocks are skewed you'll hit race conditions. we added a 30s clock skew tolerance and refresh at 70% of lifetime.

kevin: proposing a small SDK enhancement: expose a boolean flag 'reconnectOnRefresh' on streaming clients so users can opt into automatic reconnect when auth is rotated. filed issue #4523 and added a tiny PoC. pinging @tariq for review.

maria: nice. can we also clarify which JWT claim the server uses for org/project mapping? i've seen both `iss` and `sub` used in different IDPs.

tariq: we map by issuer (`iss`) + configured org allowlist. reason: `sub` can be token-specific (e.g., token exchange may set sub to ephemeral subject). `iss` is stable and tied to the identity provider or service account issuer. i'll add test coverage for both but recommend using `iss` as the canonical issuer for org scoping.

devops-bot: :information_source: deploy-report: canary rollout of devex-js@0.9.8 in staging — includes 'reconnectOnRefresh' behind feature flag `stream_reconnect_on_refresh`.

jen: tested in staging for 24h, streams reconnect cleanly, no token leak. will run end-to-end with our idp tomorrow and report.

maria: thanks everyone — i'll update our onboarding doc with the aud/iss guidance and the reconnect pattern, and i'll link the PR. @tariq i'll add you to the review request for #4523. :thumbsup:
